summary: Bank of America operates as a financial holding company providing a diversified range of banking, investing, asset management, and risk management products and services. The company serves individual consumers, small- and middle-market businesses, institutional investors, large corporations, and governments through six specific business segments: Deposits, Card Services, Consumer Real Estate Services, Global Commercial Banking, Global Banking & Markets, and Global Wealth & Investment Management, with remaining operations recorded in All Other. These segments deliver services through banking and various nonbanking subsidiaries located throughout the United States and in international markets. The company's principal executive offices are located in Charlotte, North Carolina, and its website provides access to its annual reports and corporate governance materials.

EOG Resources, Inc. explores for, develops, produces, and markets natural gas, crude oil, condensate, and natural gas liquids primarily in the United States, Canada, offshore Trinidad, and the United Kingdom North Sea. The company operates through exploration and production segments focusing on major basins such as the Barnett Shale, Permian Basin, Rocky Mountains, and Gulf of Mexico. Its customers include the National Gas Company of Trinidad and Tobago for natural gas sales and the Petroleum Company of Trinidad and Tobago for condensate and crude oil sales. EOG also sells natural gas to local Trinidadian markets under take-or-pay contracts. The company sells its natural gas production to customers including NGC, Caribbean Nitrogen Company Limited, Nitrogen (2000) Unlimited, and an unnamed methanol plant in Trinidad, as well as on the spot market. EOG also sells its crude oil and condensate production to various purchasers at market-responsive prices. The segment details specific take-or-pay contracts supplying natural gas to ammonia and LNG plants in Trinidad, while noting that United Kingdom production is sold on the spot market. Additionally, the company holds non-operating working interests in North Sea gas fields, though these are described as investments rather than active sales operations. The company's strategy involves maximizing return on investment by controlling costs and utilizing advanced technologies to enhance production rates and reserve replacement. Sales occur through various mechanisms, including market prices, long-term contracts with fixed or index-based pricing, spot markets, and specific financial instruments like collars.

ServiceNow is a leading provider of cloud-based, Software-as-a-Service applications designed to automate and manage IT service relationships across global enterprises. The company offers a suite of IT Service Automation Applications, including Incident, Problem, Change, and Release Management, alongside Custom Application Development tools that allow users to build business applications with minimal coding. It also provides expert services such as professional implementation, training, certification, and 24/7 technical support. ServiceNow operates on a multi-instance architecture, delivering these services through a proprietary platform accessible via the Internet. The company primarily markets its services to large enterprises in diverse industries, including financial services, consumer products, IT services, health care, and technology. As of December 31, 2013, the company had 2,061 customers, with no single customer accounting for more than 10% of revenue.

Copart, Inc. is a leading provider of vehicle remarketing services across the United States, Canada, and the United Kingdom, processing and selling vehicles primarily through its Virtual Bidding Second Generation auction-style sales technology. The company acquires, processes, and sells salvage vehicles, including damaged and recovered stolen vehicles, to maximize proceeds for sellers while offering a comprehensive suite of services such as Internet-based auctions, online bidding, vehicle dismantling parts locator tools, and specialized sales for motorcycles, boats, and rental cars. Its primary customers include insurance companies, banks, financial institutions, charities, car dealerships, fleet operators, rental companies, and the general public, with the firm also facilitating sales for trade-ins through dealer programs. In North America, Copart operates principally as an agent charging transaction and service fees for towing and storage, whereas in the UK, it functions on a principal basis by purchasing salvage vehicles outright and reselling them. The company provides value-added services to expedite sales and minimize administrative costs, including coverage for global buyer access, local inspection stations, prompt disaster response, title processing, and electronic communication, alongside estimating services and real-time reporting tools to assist sellers in claims evaluation and vehicle disposition.

NYSE Euronext, Inc. was formed on May 22, 2006, as a wholly owned subsidiary resulting from the combination of NYSE Group and Euronext N.V. The company has not conducted any material activities other than those incidental to its formation and the matters contemplated by the Combination Agreement. Consequently, the entity describes no products, services, business segments, or customers. NYSE Group and Euronext will continue to operate separately under their respective brand names after the combination is completed.

PG&E Corporation operates as an energy holding company with a primary subsidiary, the Utility, which provides electricity and natural gas distribution and transmission services throughout Northern and Central California. The Utility serves two main customer groups: core customers, who are primarily residential and smaller commercial entities receiving bundled services, and noncore customers, who are mostly industrial and larger commercial clients purchasing gas from marketers while using the Utility for transmission and distribution. Additionally, PG&E National Energy Group (NEG) functions as an integrated energy company offering power generation, new plant development, natural gas transmission, and wholesale energy marketing and trading across North America. NEG's specific customers include power plant developers, natural gas transmission clients, and wholesale energy buyers. The Utility remains the dominant segment, while NEG's operations focus on generation assets and wholesale markets outside traditional regulated distribution territories. Pacific Gas and Electric Company provides regulated electric and gas distribution and transmission services in Northern and Central California, covering approximately 70,000 square miles with an estimated population of 13 million across 48 counties. The company serves residential, small commercial, and other customer classes within this diverse economy. The National Energy Group, Inc. businesses operate wholesale power sales, natural gas transmission, and hydroelectric and pumped storage projects, selling power to independent power producers and other utilities, transporting natural gas in interstate commerce, and managing generation facilities subject to federal and state regulations. Pacific Gas and Electric Company operates as a utility serving approximately 4.6 million electric distribution customers, including residential, commercial, industrial, agricultural, and public street lighting clients. The company sells electric energy through various channels, primarily providing service to customers who remain with the utility as their supplier, while also facilitating a direct access market where customers can purchase power directly from competing non-utility retail electric providers or negotiate contracts with electric generators. The utility provides these third-party suppliers with billing options and energy credits, but does not sell energy directly to these direct access customers. The segment details the utility's generation resources, including hydroelectric, nuclear, and fossil-fueled plants, which supply the electricity delivered to its retail customer base. Pacific Gas and Electric Company operates an integrated electric utility business in California, providing electricity generation, transmission, and distribution services. The company sells electric energy to residential, commercial, industrial, and other gas utility customers and offers transmission and distribution services as separate products to industrial and larger commercial gas customers.
